draft.title: Exact values
card: Half a square with side 1 has angles π/4, π/4 and π/2. By Pythagoras the hypotenuse is √2. So sin(π/4) = 1/√2, cos(π/4) = 1/√2 and tan(π/4) = 1.
Half an equilateral triangle with side 2 has angles π/6, π/3 and π/2. Its short side is 1 and its other side is √3, by Pythagoras.
Opposite π/6 is 1, so sin(π/6) = 1/2, cos(π/6) = √3/2 and tan(π/6) = 1/√3. Opposite π/3 is √3, so sin(π/3) = √3/2, cos(π/3) = 1/2 and tan(π/3) = √3.
Leave answers as surds, not decimals. Example: sin(π/3) × cos(π/6) = (√3/2) × (√3/2) = 3/4.
draft.remember: Draw the special triangle, then read the ratio from its sides.

a.q: Find the exact value of cos(π/3).
a.why: In the π/6, π/3, π/2 triangle, the side next to π/3 is 1 and the hypotenuse is 2, so cos(π/3) = 1/2. The value √3/2 is tempting, but that is sin(π/3) and cos(π/6).
a.clue: Which side is next to the angle π/3?

b.why: sin(π/6) = 1/2 and tan(π/4) = 1, so the sum is 1/2 + 1 = 3/2. The option 1/2 is tempting, but it leaves out the tan(π/4) term.
b.clue: Find each value from its triangle, then add.
